title: Direct interaction of Vδ7 TCRs with IL17RA drives the differentiation of TH1-like γδT cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and decompressed the only public data file, GSE292182_BEKO_RNA_tpm.txt.gz (572 KB), from the NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) FTP site: it is a plain tab-separated table with 25,629 gene rows and exactly 4 numeric columns (TPM_1..TPM_4, i.e. transcripts per million). Confirmed via GEO and SRA (Sequence Read Archive) that the linked BioProject PRJNA1237343 contains only 4 sequencing runs, and that the GEO series lists only 4 samples (BEKO high density and low density, 2 replicates each). Searched GEO, BioProject, Zenodo and Dryad for any companion T-cell-receptor repertoire or single-cell deposit and found none; the PubMed record lists no databank accessions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology (IL17RA as a γδ T-cell receptor ligand, the Vδ7 germline-encoded contact, the diverse CDR3 repertoire, TH1-like effector program) comes from the abstract alone. The paper is not open access, has no PubMed Central identifier and no full text in Europe PMC, so the methods, the data availability statement and the supplementary tables (which likely hold the repertoire sequencing and binding measurements) were never seen.

a1_downloadable.note: The one public file downloads freely from GEO without login; verified by downloading it.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target of any kind is in the file: it holds only gene-level expression values for 4 samples. Any label of interest (does this Vδ7 receptor bind IL17RA? is this cell TH1-like?) would have to be constructed from data that is not deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: The proposed inputs — T-cell receptor CDR3 (complementarity-determining region 3) sequences — are absent. The file contains gene symbols and numbers, no sequences.

a4_units_stated.note: Column header says TPM (transcripts per million); units are explicit and consistent across all 4 columns.

a5_enough_rows.note: The unit of analysis is the sample, and there are 4 (2 conditions x 2 replicates). The 25,629 gene rows are features of those 4 samples, not independent labelled examples. Far below the ~400 minimum.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 572 KB gzipped, ~3 MB uncompressed; verified by downloading.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO metadata (4 samples), SRA (4 runs) and the file (4 columns) all agree; the paper's own count could not be checked because there is no open full text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable because there is no label. The physically measured quantities behind the paper's claims (receptor binding, flow-cytometry phenotypes, repertoire sequencing) were not deposited anywhere I could find.

existing_models.name: TCRBinder (2025, PLOS Computational Biology) — a deep model for T-cell receptor binding specificity built on ESM-2 (a protein language model) and Roformer encoders
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors to surpass leading tools on benchmark and independent datasets; exact numbers and splits not retrieved (search result summary only).

existing_models.name: Benchmark of 50 T-cell-receptor–epitope binding predictors (2025, Nature Methods)
existing_models.score_and_split: Covers 21 datasets, 762 epitopes; found that the source of negative examples strongly changes apparent accuracy and that performance rises with more receptors per epitope.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Choice of negative examples and generalisation to epitopes with few known binders remain unsolved (per the search summary).

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would be the natural backbone for a receptor-sequence task
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for the small checkpoints

integration.partner_dataset: VDJdb / IMGT (international ImMunoGeneTics information system) reference germline sequences
integration.join_key: V-gene name (e.g. TRDV7) and CDR3 amino-acid sequence
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be made useful, because this paper deposits no receptor sequences to join on.

controls.positive_control: None available: with 4 samples there is nothing to hold out.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=4.
controls.external_validation: None; no second source of the same measurement was found.

honest_claim_h3: With only a 4-sample expression table in hand, no model trained on this paper's public data could claim anything beyond 'these two culture densities differ in expression', which a t-test already says.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gamma-delta T-cell receptor sequence to predict whether it binds the IL17RA receptor and drives a TH1-like fate.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: the amino-acid sequence of each gamma-delta T-cell receptor (its V-gene identity plus the variable CDR3 loop). Number of such receptors in the public data: zero — none are deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: binds IL17RA or not, and whether the cell takes a TH1-like (interferon-gamma producing) program. The true answer would come from the paper's binding assays and flow cytometry, neither of which was deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gamma-delta T cells are the one lymphocyte class whose antigen recognition rules are unknown, so any sequence-to-ligand rule would be genuinely new; immunology labs working on gamma-delta cell therapy would use it. None of that is reachable from this deposit.

more_or_better_data.why: The public deposit is 4 bulk RNA-sequencing samples; existing receptor-binding models are trained on tens of thousands of receptor–epitope pairs from VDJdb, IEDB and McPAS.

confidence_score.why: Two replicates per condition cannot support per-prediction confidence estimates for anything.

models_beatable.why: The named models are 2025-vintage and language-model based; more importantly there is no data here to train a competitor on.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model would not see everything the baseline sees, because this paper contributes no receptor sequences at all.

ml_idea: The attractive idea was to learn which gamma-delta T-cell receptor sequences engage IL17RA, using ESM-2 embeddings of the Vδ7 chain plus CDR3 and the paper's binding/differentiation readouts as labels. It is not executable: the only public data is a 4-sample gene-expression table with no sequences and no outcome column.

effort.compute_note: Measured directly: the single file is 572 KB gzipped and loads into pandas in under a second; no other data exists to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the samples in GEO series GSE292182 — it says 4. That one number kills the project in under a minute, and it did.

verdict_reason: The entire public dataset is one 4-sample, 25,629-gene expression table (verified by download); no receptor sequences, no binding or phenotype labels, nothing to model.
